name: respond.io
summary: Shared inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS, email and live chat, with workflow automation, broadcasts and AI agents on top. The catch is where the line sits: automation, broadcasts, AI agents and the API all start at Growth, so the entry plan is the inbox without the engine.
best_for: a small team that already lives in WhatsApp and Instagram DMs and has outgrown a shared phone — retail, clinics, travel, local services. Per-contact pricing suits you if headcount grows faster than conversation volume, and the seven-day trial without a card lets you check that before committing
skip_if: you only need one channel: a plain shared inbox or a helpdesk will cost less than an omnichannel platform you use a fifth of. Skip the Starter plan specifically if automation is the reason you are looking — you will be on Growth within a month. And if your monthly active contacts run into the tens of thousands, get the number in writing first, because that is the meter and the published ladder stops being informative
honest_knock: The entry plan is the inbox without the engine. At $79 you get shared inboxes across WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS and live chat, and that alone solves the “five people answering from one phone” problem. But workflow automation, broadcasts, AI Agents and the API — the things most people picture when they read “omnichannel platform” — begin at $159, so the real entry price for an automated setup is double the headline. Work out which side of that line you sit on before comparing it with anything else. And note the meter: you pay per active contact per month, so cost follows how many people message you, not how many staff you add. That is kinder than per-seat pricing for a small team fielding a lot of chats, and harsher if you have a big list you talk to often.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (2026-08-13, read off respond.io/pricing) Four tiers, billed on monthly active contacts rather than seats: Starter $79/month, Growth $159, Advanced $279, and Enterprise on quote. Paying yearly takes roughly 20% off — $948, $1,908 and $3,348 a year against $1,188, $2,388 and $4,188 monthly. The trial is 7 days and takes no card. What separates the tiers is not volume but capability, and the line matters: Starter buys team and custom inboxes, the mobile app, AI Prompt, AI Assist, basic reports and 2FA. **Workflows automation, broadcasts, AI Agents, advanced reports, the developer API and the Zapier and Make integrations all start at Growth.** Advanced adds multiple workspaces, SSO, webhooks, HTTP requests in workflows and phone-number masking, and although a figure is shown its button says “Talk to Sales”. One thing we could not pin down. The page carries a selector for 1,000 / 2,500 / 5,000 / 10,000 / more than 10,000 monthly active contacts under the heading “pay only for the contacts you talk to”, but the prices we read did not move between those settings. Ask what your contact volume actually costs before you sign — that is the meter you are buying. Re-verified 11 October 2026 on respond.io/pricing: the yearly totals ($948, $1,908, $3,348) and the monthly totals ($1,188, $2,388, $4,188) are unchanged. Read them carefully: the $79, $159 and $279 shown per month are the yearly rates, and the page data gives $99, $199 and $349 for month-to-month billing. The plan comparison now lists users per tier — 5 on Starter, 10 on Growth and Advanced, extra users at $12, $20 and $24 a month on yearly billing ($15, $25 and $30 monthly) — plus AI Credits of 5,000, 10,000, 20,000 and 40,000. In that same table Starter shows unlimited monthly active contacts, while Growth and Advanced 'start with 1,000', so the contact meter applies from Growth up. The trial gives Growth features for 5 users and 1,000 contacts, without broadcasts.

compare_with.name: Wati
compare_with.why: the comparison most WhatsApp-first teams will make, and one we have already researched. Both put a shared team inbox on top of the WhatsApp Business API; the practical difference is how the meter runs and where automation starts. respond.io reaches wider across channels — Instagram, Messenger, SMS, live chat and email in the same inbox — which is worth paying for only if you genuinely answer on more than one

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 31 October 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We tried to import two made-up contacts from CSV, added them by hand instead, exported them and looked at the paid plans.
findings: The trial was 7 days on the Growth plan, with no card. The phone number at sign-up is optional.
The CSV import says email, phone or contact ID can identify contacts, but it would not continue until a phone number column was mapped. Our test file had none.
The import mapping offered only standard fields such as name, phone, email, tags and lifecycle.
Adding the two contacts by hand worked. The CSV export kept the names with accents and the email addresses, but merged first and last name and had no contact ID.
Starter was $99 a month and Growth $199. Choosing Starter lists the Growth features you would lose, such as AI Agents, Workflows and the Developer API.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
